title: What washes up on beaches: cigarette butts, bottle caps, foam, lost fishing gear, and plastic bags

sources.title: What is the most common form of ocean litter?

facts.text: Cigarette butts are the most common kind of litter collected in beach and coastal cleanups.
Most cigarette filters are made of cellulose acetate, a plastic-like material.
Sunlight can break the filter fibers into smaller and smaller pieces, but the pieces do not disappear.
Plastic items such as bottle caps, food wrappers, and plastic bags are common types of marine debris.
Animals can mistake pieces of debris for food and swallow them.
Sea turtles often try to eat plastic bags and sheets, which can look like the jellyfish they eat.
Lost or abandoned fishing gear is one of the most harmful types of marine debris.
Lost fishing gear can keep trapping fish, sea turtles, and seabirds, and synthetic gear can stay in the sea for many years.
